title: Configure persistent macOS signing for Cell
summary: Inspect or explicitly create or select Cell's shared native production certificate and preserve stable product identifiers without routine CI changing the signer.
use_when: Inspect Cell's selected macOS signing certificate and current key usability.
Create the initial local certificate or explicitly select an existing certificate or namespace.
Understand signing identity continuity, CI signing requirements, native product coverage, or deliberate certificate rotation.
do_not_use_when: Only submit or inspect a CI job without changing signing configuration; use the queue contract.
Developer ID distribution, notarization, package-installer signing, new entitlements, or native identity for a Python interpreter or standalone script is required.
Automatically replace an unavailable certificate, bypass active work, or infer that signing grants macOS permissions.
outcome: The current user's fixed signing configuration selects one exact usable certificate and permanent identifier namespace, or inspection returns its current readiness without changing configuration.

interfaces.label: Inspect selection and current key usability
Read structured selection and current key usability
Run signing setup before manager replacement

effects: Status reads host configuration, queries macOS code-signing identities, and performs a dry-run signature; it does not change signing configuration or product selection.

Initial creation generates one RSA 3072-bit self-signed code-signing certificate with SHA-256 signature and 3650-day validity, imports its certificate and key into the login Keychain, authorizes /usr/bin/codesign for that key, and adds current-user code-signing trust. macOS can require native user authorization.

Initial creation uses private temporary staging for generation files and removes them when setup exits. It retains the certificate and private key in Keychain, with no retained certificate or private-key export in the host filesystem.

Explicit configuration preflights the exact selected certificate and private key before atomically writing the normalized fixed host signing policy. Configuration writers serialize with queue and deployment admission and refuse unsettled work.
Production preparation signs and verifies staged native executables before sealing. CI, cache reuse, upgrades, and installation read the policy without changing it.
authority: The user owns explicit certificate and namespace selection. Cell owns policy validation, snapshot retention, identifier derivation, and publication checks. macOS Keychain owns private-key storage and use authorization.
New CI jobs and deployment operations use their retained signing snapshot. A policy mismatch stops publication instead of choosing a current or alternative identity.

The filesystem and current-user operating boundary protects configuration from routine source, cache and repair writes. It is not a security boundary against arbitrary hostile code with full current-user authority.
success: Status reports the selected fingerprint, namespace, Keychain and readiness only after the exact certificate and private-key preflight succeeds. With --json it returns policy and ready=true.

Initial creation reports the selected fingerprint, namespace and Keychain after certificate import, trust setup, key-use preflight and private configuration publication. With --json it returns policy.

Explicit configure reports the selected fingerprint, namespace and Keychain after preflight and atomic configuration publication. With --json it returns policy. Configuration selection alone does not prove that every product was redeployed.

Production success requires native signatures and declared inventory matching the retained policy and preparation. Full adoption or rotation additionally requires the full intended product rollout and its retained outcome.
failure_and_recovery: Missing configuration, inaccessible or expired identity, locked Keychain, wrong signer, or failed verification stops admission or publication with no unsigned, ad hoc, certificate-name, generated-identity or renewal fallback. Signing configuration failures do not invoke model repair.

Creation refuses existing configuration or a Cell Local Signing certificate in the selected login Keychain. Partial setup can leave a Keychain import without configuration; use configure to select that existing identity after its key is usable. Creation never silently replaces it.

Configuration failure preserves the previous file. An unavailable selected certificate or key blocks signing until that identity is usable or the user explicitly configures another identity. Verify status before admission resumes.
Reissuing a certificate with the same key changes its fingerprint and requires explicit selection. Existing immutable releases are not re-signed in place.

Rotation is an explicit configuration change followed by selected product deployment. Sequential installation can leave more than one signer after a failed rollout; inspect retained outcomes before claiming fleet completion.
privacy: The private signing.json retains certificate fingerprint, Keychain path, profile and namespace; job and preparation receipts retain those public signing inputs, not private-key material.
The certificate and private key remain in macOS Keychain after setup. Generation files stay in private temporary staging and are removed when setup exits; no filesystem export is retained.
Signing commands return public selection, policy and readiness only. Private-key bytes and passwords do not enter CI repair requests, command diagnostics, or signing status output.
does_not_authorize: Creating or changing an identity from status inspection, catalog discovery, ordinary CI submission, installation, cache cleanup, or model repair alone.
Cancelling jobs, removing locks, clearing deployment recovery, overwriting foreign Keychain content, or changing another product's permission or entitlement boundary.
Disclosing private-key bytes or passwords, publishing a distribution artifact, or claiming Developer ID, notarization, Gatekeeper or perpetual permission continuity.

consumers.statement: The current user and authorized Cell operators can inspect readiness, perform initial local signing setup, and deliberately select a certificate or namespace.
Routine CI repair and installation are not certificate-selection or key-generation consumers.

preconditions.statement: Signing setup and configuration require macOS, the current user's Keychain, the configured external Cell work volume, and available /usr/bin/security, /usr/bin/codesign and /usr/bin/openssl. Key import, use and trust can require native user authorization.

Configuration mutation requires paused CI, no active or queued jobs, no release-publication lock, and no live or retained unresolved deployment. Writers hold queue admission and deployment locks. Status can run without those maintenance conditions.

inputs.statement: Status and create-local take no signing-selection overrides. Configure accepts exactly a 40-hexadecimal-digit certificate SHA-1 fingerprint, an absolute user-owned regular Keychain path, and a dotted lowercase identifier namespace defaulting to local.cell. Each subcommand accepts --json for structured output. This release supports profile local and policy schema 1 only.
Certificate-name selection, per-product signer overrides, environment signer overrides, automatic renewal and ad hoc production signing are unsupported.

outputs.statement: Commands default to text showing the selected fingerprint, namespace and Keychain; status also reports readiness after preflight. With --json, status returns policy and ready=true, while configure and create-local return policy. Operational failure returns exit 78 with a diagnostic; syntax errors return exit 2.

The fixed host signing.json contains schema 1 and macos profile, normalized certificate_sha1, absolute keychain and identifier_namespace. Creation retains the certificate and private key in Keychain and removes private temporary generation files when setup exits.

data_semantics.statement: The configured certificate fingerprint selects the exact leaf certificate and private key; it does not name an executable-content hash algorithm. Keychain path changes relocate that selection, fingerprint changes rotate it, and namespace changes alter code identifiers.
A ready status is a successful current usability probe, not a promise of later Keychain access or an installed-fleet signing audit.

identity_and_units.statement: Certificate identity is a normalized lowercase SHA-1 fingerprint. Cell compares normalized policy objects directly. Code identifiers are NAMESPACE.PRODUCT.EXECUTABLE using canonical krisis identity for the decisions descriptor and permanent declared binary names; build paths and source versions do not enter them.

Initial creation uses RSA 3072 bits, SHA-256 certificate signature and 3650-day validity. The designated requirement pins the exact identifier and leaf certificate. Local production signing requests no network timestamp.

completeness_and_freshness.statement: Production coverage is every Cell-native production executable declared in selected products' inventory: commands, daemons, helpers and installers. Full-inventory adoption and rotation require explicit full product selection; ordinary selective CI remains selective.

Standalone scripts, Python CI-manager process identity, tests, compiler scratch outputs and third-party runtimes are outside Cell-native identity coverage. Package manifests and owned file paths retain their existing asset coverage.
No continual readiness observation, key-usability lifetime, full installed-fleet status audit, or macOS permission-prompt suppression is promised.

access.statement: The supported local interface is cell-ci signing status, create-local and configure. Before updated manager installation, the source ci_manager/client.py exposes the same subcommands. The root signing wrapper selects installed code. Configuration stays outside Git, worktrees and release caches.

The fixed current-user signing.json must be an owned non-symbolic mode-0600 file; signing state directories use mode 0700. The Keychain retains private-key authority. The manager supplies repair agents no private-key material or signing configuration writer.

lifecycle_and_consistency.statement: Explicit configuration preflights the selected identity before atomic replacement. Creation refuses existing configuration or a named Cell Local Signing certificate in the selected login Keychain. Ordinary build, CI, repair, install, manager upgrade and cache reuse never mutate signing selection. New jobs retain policy at admission; legacy jobs without a snapshot retain their earlier path.

Staged native artifacts are signed, externally verified against the expected signer and identifier, then sealed. Retained candidates and pre-acceptance production receipts are reverified. A changed policy after admission stops publication. Immutable historical releases retain their original bytes.
Explicit rotation requires drained maintenance and a full intended product rollout. Product installation is sequential; an interrupted rollout does not establish one fleet-wide signer.

operational_limits.statement: The supported profile is local signing with no new entitlement or Hardened Runtime options. The exact configured identity must be usable for every new macOS production preparation. No certificate rotation or renewal occurs automatically.

Developer ID distribution, notarization, package-installer certificates, native script/interpreter identity, fleet-wide atomic rotation, retrospective release re-signing and hosted private-key escrow are not supported.
No perpetual certificate usability, completion deadline, fleet size limit or future macOS permission behavior is promised.

compatibility_and_evolution.statement: Manager release 0.7.0 publishes signing contract 2 and policy schema 1. Unsupported schemas, profiles or fields fail closed. Manager replacement preserves the fixed host signing configuration and retained job snapshots. Jobs without a signing snapshot do not acquire one.
No automatic signing-policy migration, certificate renewal, future profile support or deprecation interval is promised.

reliances.statement: Certificate import, code-signing trust, private-key authorization and signature evaluation rely on macOS Security and Keychain tools. No dedicated installed Chancery contract covers this operating-system boundary.
Initial key generation and self-signed certificate creation rely on the host OpenSSL command. No dedicated installed Chancery contract covers that executable.

Publication, cache retention and sequential product rollout rely on Cell's release builder, coordinator and product installers. Their retained operation evidence remains authoritative and has no dedicated coordinator Chancery contract.
